body:
## Problem

Support staff on a read-only impersonation session cannot size a workflow audience: the count never loads and the request fails with `403 impersonation_read_only`. That is every audience-sizing read in the workflow builder while impersonating.

- `ImpersonationReadOnlyMiddleware` blocks every non-idempotent method during a read-only session.
- `POST hog_flows/user_blast_radius` carries its filters in the body, because they are too large for a query string.
- The middleware rejects it before it reaches the viewset, so the endpoint's own permissions never run.

## Changes

- The audience count now loads during read-only impersonation, through one entry in `READ_ONLY_IMPERSONATION_ALLOWLISTED_PATHS`.
- The regex names the single action, so the writing actions under the same `hog_flows/` prefix stay blocked.
- Nothing about the endpoint changes, and no other surface changes.

The action is safe to allowlist because it only reads. It counts matching persons or groups, reads the team's batch trigger limit, and returns a `TimestampSigner` signature as the confirm token. The audience helpers under `products/workflows/backend/services/` hold no write. The endpoints that spend the confirm token (`run`, `batch_jobs`) stay blocked, so a read-only session still cannot dispatch a send.

The alternative was to declare read-only actions on the viewset and have the middleware consult that. The allowlist is deliberately fail-closed and security-reviewed, so a platform change to how "read-only" is decided belongs in its own PR, not behind a support fix.

No visual change: the fix restores a count that already has its own UI.

## How did you test this code?

- Added one case to the existing `test_read_only_impersonation_allows_allowlisted_post` list, rather than a new test.
- The case catches the regression where an edit to the allowlist regex stops matching this path and support sessions get the 403 again. It failed with the entry removed and passed with it in place.
- Added two cases to `test_read_only_impersonation_blocks_mutating_siblings`: `hog_flows/<id>/publish/` and `hog_flows/bulk_delete/`.
- Those two catch the opposite regression: a later edit widening the regex to the `hog_flows/` prefix would hand a read-only session a workflow write.
- Checked directly that the committed regex matches the audience path with and without the trailing slash, and rejects `publish`, `bulk_delete`, and the bare prefix.
- Not run: pytest after the master merge. The local virtualenv has protobuf runtime 5.29.6 against gencode 6.31.1, so Django cannot import, and the machine has too little disk to rebuild the environment. The allowed-path case did run before the merge, and failed with the allowlist entry removed. CI runs the suite.

## Docs update

None. The allowlist is internal and carries its own comment.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5

Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/simplify`, `/reviewing-with-coderabbit`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`.

CodeRabbit CLI pass: ran over the branch against master, 0 findings. This CLI version (0.7.6) has no `--deep` flag, so the run used the default full policy.

Greptile finding, P2, on the test list: no case proved the workflow writes stay blocked, so a later widening of the regex would go uncaught. Fixed, with the two blocked-sibling cases above. The sibling PR [#105805](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/105805) carries the same guard for feature flags.

The session started from a failing endpoint, not from this file. Reading the viewset ruled out its scopes and access checks, which left the middleware as the only layer that could answer before the action ran. Tracing the audience helpers confirmed the action writes nothing, which is what makes the allowlist entry correct rather than convenient.

Two things a reviewer may want to decide separately. The sibling `POST feature_flags/user_blast_radius` has the same shape and is still blocked; it is left alone because it was not the reported failure. The `environments` alternative in the regex matches the other entries' style, and holds either way, because `EnvironmentsRewriteMiddleware` rewrites `request.path` to `/api/projects/...` in place.

No duplicate: `gh pr list --state open --search` over impersonation, allowlist and blast radius terms found no PR fixing this. [#105805](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/105805) now fixes the feature flags sibling, which this PR deliberately leaves alone.

Public artifact: nothing here comes from the session's non-public context. The report arrived as a project URL, which appears nowhere in the diff or this description.
